text:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty: P1 GPU host flapping (host-us-west1-gpu-43) — multiple node reboots in last 12m. Paging oncall.

Mia R.: I'm on it. seeing a spike in `pci` errors and GPU driver resets across pods on that host. Some customers hit 5xx generator errors.

Samir: adding first-pass logs. look at dmesg from the host:
```
[ 12345.678901] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: id 00e0
[ 12345.678912] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: GPU reset client detected non-responsive GPU, resetting
[ 12346.123456] kernel: nvlink: link recovery detected on GPU 1
[ 12346.123460] kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: recovered from error, continuing
```
Samir: ECC counters are rising after high token throughput bursts (batching spikes at ~02:10).

AJ: curious — is this full host GPU panic or a per-GPU reset? kubelet logs show pods got ContainerStatus:OOMKilled? or just GPU reset exit?

Mia R.: Pods exit code is 137 sometimes but logs show `GPU device lost` before container termination. not clean OOM.

Tim (oncall): I'll cordon + drain the host and re-schedule affected pods to another GPU pool. Do we want to evict immediately?

Leila: early customer impact: 6 customers with >10% request error rate in the affected cluster for the 02:05–02:20 window. I'll open a CS ticket and post a status.

Samir: running serial-port output and listing kernel oops for later:
```
gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output host-us-west1-43 --zone=us-west1-b --port=1 | tail -n 200
-- shows GPU reset, then host reboot at 02:12:03 UTC
```

Samir: also `smartctl` and host event logs show no drive errors. No thermal alarms. Perf counters show sustained PCIe AER increments.

AJ: hypothesis: either firmware/driver regression or noisy neighbor causing PCIe link flaps. Provider-side NIC/PCIe soft-errors have been the root cause before. Also possible ML inference workload sending sustained large batches triggering a timing edge-case.

Mia R.: Mitigation done: host cordoned, workloads scheduled to `gpu-pool-fallback`. We disabled bursting autoscaler on that pool to avoid compounding load. Monitoring shows error rate dropping after migration.

CloudOps Bot: opened provider case C-2456789 with GCP. Included serial logs, dmesg, time ranges, and traces. Case link: https://internal.ticket/2456789

Leila: timeline so far (quick):
- 02:05 UTC — first PCIe AER spike, driver reset reported
- 02:07 UTC — multiple pods report `GPU device lost`
- 02:10 UTC — host reboot observed (automated kernel panic/reboot)
- 02:12 UTC — host back, second reset sequence at 02:12:45
- 02:17 UTC — cordon + drain initiated
- 02:22 UTC — workloads running on fallback pool, error rates falling

AJ: collecting `gpu-monitor` traces and per-pod batch size distribution. suspect batched inference windows coincide with AER bursts. Samir, can you grab `nvidia-smi -q -a` output from before the reboot (if logs exist) and attach?

Samir: attached snapshot to the ticket (link internal): /mnt/logs/host-us-west1-43/nvidia-smi-02021210.txt. counters show multiple `PCIe replay` and `link recovery` events.

Mia R.: Customer impact note for CS: customers A,B,C had degraded calls (timeouts/5xx) during 02:05–02:20. No data leak suspected. We'll offer credits if SLA thresholds breached.

Tim (oncall): For immediate in-incident mitigations we did: cordon/drain host, move critical customers to reserved `dedicated-us-west1` pool, disabled burst autoscaling for fallback pool, and opened provider case. Who's taking the RCA?

AJ: I'll own the RCA doc. Plan: gather kernel oops, serial output, nv-hostmgr logs, provider side logs, and reproduce with smaller scale workload in a staging host if provider gives a repro window.

Leila: action items for next 24h:
- AJ -> RCA doc + initial hypothesis list (firmware vs driver vs noisy neighbor)
- Samir -> attach all host-level logs + perf counters to ticket C-2456789
- Mia R. -> update CS + affected customers with incident summary and mitigation steps
- Tim -> decide on host replacement or repro step with provider after provider feedback

Samir: quick note — kernel shows `pcieport` resets targeted at downstream switch, not root complex. Means link between host port and GPU is flapping rather than host southbridge. tends to be hardware or PCIe microcode.

AJ: also adding `kubelet` eviction timeline and pod restart counts into RCA doc. Will add graphs for token throughput correlated with AER events.

Mia R.: leaving a formal handoff to Samir who will be on next shift. I'll be reachable if provider pulls logs.

Samir: taking next-shift ownership. I'll push a follow-up here once provider responds and after we run a repro.

CloudOps Bot: provider case update received: "Investigating PCIe telemetry and host firmware — requested serial logs and host config." ETA 12–24h.

Leila: tagging CS to hold on customer comms until we have root-cause confidence. Send interim message now: short status + mitigation + ETA for RCA.

Mia R.: Interim message posted to customers + internal status page. Link: https://status.redwood-inference/internal/incident/1977654321

Tim (oncall): closing the active pager for now. Keep thread updated. If host flaps again, escalate to infra-sre oncall and consider taking that host out of rotation permanently until replacement.

Samir: will also set up a long-running metric alert: if ECC corrections on a host increase > threshold in 10m window, auto-evacuate. raising that as a follow-on improvement.

Mia R.: Thanks everyone. tagging follow-ups in RCA doc.

incidents-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged and transitioned to mitigation.

(leila) NOTE: We'll collect all artifacts into the RCA doc and post summary once validated by provider.
